headline: Medium-risk pair: shared browser/file workflows can create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error paths; no direct evidence of a tighter coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and use runtime-injected MCPs/hooks; Agent B processes PDF files in a browser-based worker. That creates a plausible path where A passes untrusted content into B or vice versa through files/browser content. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Agent A writes browser-derived content into a PDF or shared file that Agent B opens
IF Agent B treats file contents as instructions rather than inert document text
mitigations: Disable automatic opening of untrusted PDFs in Agent B
Require manual review before Agent A hands content to Agent B
Use separate directories for A and B inputs
Strip instructions from extracted text before passing between agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all cross-agent file handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches project code, session history, and provider authentication data and has broad network egress; Agent B handles PDF files locally with no egress. If they share a workspace, A can expose sensitive local data into B's document-processing flow. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly documented, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF Agent A and Agent B share the same filesystem workspace
IF sensitive files from Agent A are opened or indexed by Agent B
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Remove secrets from any files B can read
Disable network egress for A during shared-document workflows
Use per-agent service accounts and credentials
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem ACL isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has broad network egress and subprocess/browser execution; Agent B can run browsers and supports multiple instances. They do not both advertise unrestricted filesystem writes, so the high-severity write-lock conflict is not proven. Still, overlapping browser/process activity can contend for shared resources if co-located, making medium the cautious choice.
conditions: IF both agents are launched against the same browser profile or temp directory
IF Agent A spawns subprocesses that modify files Agent B is reading
mitigations: Assign distinct temp directories per agent
Run only one browser-using agent per profile
Serialize file writes with a simple operator checklist
Close shared browser sessions before switching agents
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate or transform content from code, docs, and web sources; Agent B processes PDFs and may render extracted text. If B consumes A's output without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream document outputs. The profiles do not show explicit verification gates, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Agent B uses Agent A's generated text as source material
IF no human or automated verification step checks A's claims before B renders them
mitigations: Require source citations before B accepts A output
Compare A output against original PDFs manually
Use a short validation checklist for every handoff
Reject uncited factual claims from A
requires-engineering: add automated provenance and verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles provider authentication data and session history, while Agent B only touches PDF documents. The profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch between them, so a compliance breach is not established. I cite both because the risk depends on how A's sensitive data is paired with B's document flow, but the evidence is weak.
conditions: IF regulated data from Agent A is placed into PDFs processed by Agent B
IF retention or residency policies differ for those PDFs
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data into shared PDFs
Review retention settings before processing sensitive documents
Use separate storage locations for regulated and non-regulated files
Document the data class allowed for each agent
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
